findings.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` `ensure_embeddable`'s `request.referer` check is trivially spoofable by non-browser clients and combined with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is UX gating, not real access control — fine since embed content is meant to be public, but worth a comment so it's not mistaken for a security boundary later.

`TopicEmbed.import`'s check-then-create (`where(...).first` then `create!`) can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` under a race (two feed items / concurrent manual retrieve resolving to the same URL); the 60s Redis throttle and pre-existence checks reduce but don't eliminate this. Consider rescuing and retrying the lookup.

Test coverage gaps: no test for the protocol-relative URL bug (#3) or for HTML sanitization on the RSS path (#2); controller/component specs are heavily mock-based (`TopicView.expects(:new)`, etc.) rather than real integration renders — a real render of `best.html.erb` would have caught Critical #1 immediately.
`SiteSetting.embeddable_host` supports only a single host; reasonable v1 scope, just noting as a likely near-term need.
`embed.js` assumes `discourseUrl` has a trailing slash (`discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`); a misconfigured snippet without it silently breaks the widget with no error surfaced.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

Consider rescuing and retrying the lookup.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so if two workers/processes call `import` concurrently with the same `url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and then race on `create!`, causing the loser to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. The surrounding checks (`TopicRetriever` does `exists?` prechecks and uses a 60s Redis throttle) reduce the likelihood but don’t eliminate the fundamental TOCTOU race between the lookup/exists check and the insert.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally implements embedding allowlisting using a single `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` string, enforced by strict equality checks in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. This is a deliberate scope/design choice (a single allowed host), not a defect or correctness/security bug introduced by the change. The proposed finding is essentially a future enhancement note, not a verifiable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed.js` assumes `discourseUrl` has a trailing slash (`discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`); a misconfigured snippet without it silently breaks the widget with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the iframe URL is constructed via simple string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. There is no normalization to ensure exactly one `/` between the base URL and `embed/best`. If `discourseUrl` is configured as `https://forum.example.com` (no trailing slash), the result becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is an invalid endpoint and will break embedding. The diff does not show any guarantee that `discourseUrl` always ends with `/`, so this is a real robustness/correctness issue introduced by the code.
